non_blind_reason: the seed-42 single-representation reading 0.6080587938801277 and the shot-17 head sweep were known before this file was written; this is a within-family hyperparameter grid, not an external test
question: on the frozen protocol (5 folds x 10 repeats, GroupKFold by InChIKey, Physical(lever4), train_mask full_base 2029 rows, score_mask scored 457 rows / 97 compounds), does retuning the XGBoost hyperparameters of the dense physical configuration push the cross-seed endpoint above 0.60?

frozen_protocol.train_mask: full_base (2029 base rows) -- the shot-13 full_table_lever4 configuration
frozen_protocol.model_process: ProcessPoolExecutor over (repeat, fold) tasks, one fold per task, every grid arm fitted inside the same worker

grid.selection_rule: three pre-registered blocks, listed in full below; (a) 12 axis-sweep arms = the frozen reference plus one factor moved at a time (depth 3/4/6, trees 400/800, lr 0.03/0.1, min_child_weight 5, subsample 1.0, colsample 1.0, both 1.0); (b) 7 capacity-ladder arms over depth x trees x lr at the frozen regularisation; (c) 3 regularisation-relaxed arms that move min_child_weight / subsample / colsample together. The full 288-point cartesian product is explicitly not run. See cost_amendment: the arm set actually registered for the run is the 7-arm subset that carries both axes.

decision_rule.best_arm: highest cross-seed mean R2 among the non-reference arms; ties break on arm name
decision_rule.confirmed: the best non-reference arm has cross-seed mean R2 > 0.60 AND its cross-seed mean improvement over xgb_reference is >= +0.02
decision_rule.partial: the best non-reference arm has cross-seed mean improvement over xgb_reference >= +0.005 but the confirmed gate is not met
decision_rule.refuted: the best non-reference arm has cross-seed mean improvement over xgb_reference < +0.005
decision_rule.placebo: verdict is placebo when --placebo is used; the target is permuted on the scored rows only before fitting

anchors.fold_signature: must equal dielectric_pool_expansion_benchmark.fold_signature of the frozen scoreboard splits
anchors.on_mismatch: refuse to report anything else and exit non-zero

promotion_rule: no reading from this probe is promoted; the frozen headline stays 0.4766400383507876 and the frozen baseline stays 0.4091179943351143 regardless of the outcome
pre_run_correction: 2026-09-27: the first transcription of arm_params hard-coded subsample=0.8/colsample_bytree=0.8 for every arm, which contradicted the arm names and the locked grid factors; the script refused to start before any fit was run, the table was rebuilt from the arm names, and the digest was re-pinned. No result existed when this was corrected.

cost_amendment.rule: amended before the first fit; no reading of any arm existed when this was written
measurement: one frozen-head fit (200 trees, max_depth 2) on the 2029 x 2061 dense Physical(lever4)+Morgan design matrix costs 4.16 s CPU (8.04 s wall while the machine was loaded)
the deepest registered arm (800 trees, max_depth 6) costs about 35 s of CPU for the same matrix
XGBoost histogram construction is O(rows x features), so the 2048 dense ECFP columns dominate the cost and no hyper-parameter of the frozen head changes it
cost_amendment.registered_cost: 22 arms x 50 folds x 5 seeds = 5,500 fits per seed, about 18,500 s of CPU per seed, i.e. over 2.6 hours of pure CPU for the five-seed set before any process overhead
cost_amendment.preserved: both registered axes -- depth at the frozen tree count (3 / 4 / 6) and tree count at the frozen depth (400 / 800) -- plus one depth x capacity interaction point (depth 4, 400 trees)
cost_amendment.dropped: the learning-rate / min_child_weight / subsample / colsample axis variants (4.16 s per fit each, dropped for budget only) and the eight 800-tree lattice points (4x to 8x the reference cost each)
cost_amendment.unchanged: the representation, the pool, the splitter, the frozen head, the five locked seeds, the anchor and the decision rule are all untouched by this amendment
